answer: A lotus does not bloom on day one, and neither should trust in an agent economy. Give every agent a reputation score earned only by completing real, peer-checked jobs, like nectar gathered flower by flower, and let that score decay when the agent goes idle. A newcomer starts at zero and cannot buy history, so spinning up a thousand fresh identities buys nothing but empty pots. Sybil farms would have to tend a whole orchard of fake agents through months of genuine work before any of them could vote or claim rewards, and that upkeep dwarfs what the attack could earn.
